## 📌 Description This PR adds **`flashinfer.mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm`** as an **experimental API**. The op is the pre-finalize step of a manifold-constrained hyper-connection (mHC) boundary with `HC = 4` residual streams. It also fuses the next sublayer's RMSNorm into its output. On SM100 / SM103, decode batches run a new thread-block-cluster kernel. Every other call runs a composable fp32 PyTorch implementation of the same contract, so the API always returns a result. ### Model and use case - **Model:** the op was written for decode of [GLM-5.3-Flash](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4) (hidden size 4096, `hc_mult = 4`, 45 layers) on GB300. - **Call count:** every attention and every MoE sublayer is wrapped by an mHC boundary, so the op runs **90 times per decode step**. - **Current vLLM path:** for batches of up to 32 tokens, vLLM runs each boundary as two kernels: 1. `mhc_fused` mixes the sublayer output back into the 4 residual streams and computes split-K partials of the 24 mix logits. 2. A **pre-finalize** kernel, written in TileLang. It runs one 96-thread CTA per token, so a decode token's whole pre-finalize runs on a single SM. - **This PR** implements step 2. ```mermaid flowchart LR B["sublayer output
(attention or MoE)"] --> F["mhc_fused
mix into the 4 residual streams
+ split-K partials of the 24 mix logits"] F -->|"gemm_out_mul [NS, T, 24] fp32
gemm_out_sqrsum [NS, T] fp32
residual [T, 4, 4096] bf16"| P["mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm
(this PR)"] P -->|"layer_input [T, 4096] bf16
(already RMSNorm'd)"| N["next sublayer
(attention or MoE)"] P -->|"post_mix [T, 4]
comb_mix [T, 4, 4]"| F2["next boundary's
mhc_fused"] N --> F2 ``` ### What is fused ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph BEFORE["Before: stable FlashInfer APIs, two kernels"] direction LR A1["split-K partials
+ residual"] --> K1["mhc_pre_big_fuse
reduce logits → sigmoids
→ Sinkhorn → weighted sum"] K1 -->|"un-normalized layer_input
bf16, round trip through HBM"| K2["rmsnorm"] K2 --> O1["layer_input"] K1 --> M1["post_mix, comb_mix"] end subgraph AFTER["After: this PR, one kernel"] direction LR A2["split-K partials
+ residual + norm_weight"] --> K3["mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm
reduce logits → sigmoids → Sinkhorn
→ weighted sum → RMSNorm"] K3 --> O2["layer_input"] K3 --> M2["post_mix, comb_mix"] end BEFORE ~~~ AFTER ``` | step | computes | |---|---| | 1. reduce partials | `mixes = Σ_s gemm_out_mul[s] · rsqrt(Σ_s gemm_out_sqrsum[s] / (4·H) + rms_eps)` | | 2. pre | `pre = sigmoid(mixes[0:4]·hc_scale[0] + hc_base[0:4]) + hc_pre_eps` | | 3. post_mix | `post_mix = sigmoid(mixes[4:8]·hc_scale[1] + hc_base[4:8]) · hc_post_mult_value` | | 4. comb_mix | 20-iteration Sinkhorn of `softmax(mixes[8:24] as 4×4) + hc_sinkhorn_eps` | | 5. weighted sum | `ol = Σ_j pre[j] · residual[:, j, :]` (fp32) | | **6. RMSNorm (newly fused)** | `layer_input = bf16(bf16(ol) · rsqrt(mean(ol²) + norm_eps) · norm_weight)` | - Fusing the RMSNorm removes one launch and the `[T, 4096]` bf16 round trip through HBM (8 KB written and read back per token). The RMS statistic is taken on the fp32 sum `ol` rather than on its bf16 copy. - vLLM's current TileLang kernel already fuses the same six steps, but on one CTA per token. The speedups under Performance are measured against that kernel, so they come from the cluster design below, not from removing a launch. - Per token the op reads 32 KB of residual and writes 8 KB. It is latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound: on one CTA, the 20-iteration Sinkhorn chain, the 4096-wide weighted sum and the RMSNorm reduction run one after another. ### Kernel design (`mhc_pre_cluster_kernel`) ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph OLD["one CTA per token (current)"] direction TB T0["1 CTA, 96 threads, 1 SM"] --> T1["logits → sigmoids → softmax → 20× Sinkhorn"] T1 --> T2["weighted sum over 4096 channels"] T2 --> T3["RMSNorm → store"] end subgraph NEW["thread-block cluster per token (this PR)"] direction TB C0["4-CTA cluster per token
(2-CTA when T > 24)"] C0 --> R["warps 1-2 of every CTA: 1024 channels each
weighted sum + Σ ol² partial"] R --> X["all-gather of Σ ol² over DSMEM
(st.async + mbarrier)"] X --> Y["each CTA normalizes and stores its slice"] C0 --> S["warp 0 of rank 1: softmax +
division-free Sinkhorn → comb_mix"] C0 --> Q["warp 0 of the post rank:
post sigmoid → post_mix"] end ``` **Parallel layout** - The weighted sum and the RMSNorm are split across the cluster. - The only cross-CTA step is a single all-gather of the RMSNorm partial sums over distributed shared memory. - The Sinkhorn and the post sigmoid run on spare warps, concurrently with the weighted sum. - Every warp issues its global loads first, so a token costs one DRAM round trip. **Division-free Sinkhorn** - The matrix is kept in diagonal-scaling form `c = r · K · s / G`. - Cofactor products replace the per-step divisions. - The common denominator is renormalised by exact powers of two. - A single Newton-refined reciprocal produces the final `1/G`. - An exact power-of-two rebalance of `r` and `s` after every column half-step keeps both within `(2^-64, 2^50)` for every finite input. The rebalance changes no rounding. **Numerics** - The module is built without `-use_fast_math`. - `expf` is libdevice, and the post sigmoid uses IEEE division. - The pre sigmoids and `1/G` use Newton-refined reciprocals. - `rsqrt.approx` is applied only to arguments `>= 1e-5`. - fp32 add, mul and fma never flush to zero. **Launch** - One `cudaLaunchKernelEx`, with the cluster shape compiled in (`__cluster_dims__`). - Optional PDL (`enable_pdl=True`): the kernel reads no input before `griddepcontrol.wait`, and uses plain `ld.global` because `.nc` loads would be hoisted above the wait. - ptxas: 110 registers (4-CTA cluster) / 165–168 registers (2-CTA cluster), 0 spills, 112–128 B static shared memory. ### API surface All three functions are `@flashinfer_experimental_api`; calling any of them is the opt-in, and each warns once. | Function | Purpose | |---|---| | `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm(...)` | The op. Optional caller-owned outputs and `enable_pdl`. | | `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_supported(...)` | Returns True when this exact call runs the cluster kernel. A framework keeps its own path whenever it returns False. | | `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_warmup(device)` | Builds and loads the kernel before CUDA-graph capture. The kernel is never built during capture; a capturing call without a loaded module captures the composable path. | **Kernel envelope** - SM100 / SM103. - `H = 4096`, `HC = 4`, `1 <= T <= 32`, `NS ∈ {8, 64}`. - Compiled-in model constants: `rms_eps = norm_eps = 1e-5`, `hc_pre_eps = hc_sinkhorn_eps = 1e-6`, `hc_post_mult_value = 2`, `sinkhorn_repeat = 20`. The support check compares them as fp32. - Dense, 16-byte-aligned tensors. `FLASHINFER_SPECIALIZED_KERNEL_DISABLE=1`, read at call time, forces the composable path. This is the existing switch from `mla_kv_pack`; its `CLAUDE.md` row is updated. **Layout** - Core: thin entry points in `flashinfer/mhc.py` (signature, shared validation, deferred-import handoff). - Everything else lives in `flashinfer/experimental/mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm/`: kernel, JIT spec, support check, composable implementation and a README with the user contract. - JIT-only, with nothing in `aot.py`. No trace template yet. ### Performance **Kernel level** (GB300, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130) - Metric: CUPTI device time, median of 200 iterations after 20 warmup, inside CUDA-graph replay, PDL off. - *Cold*: L2 flushed before every call. *Warm*: 16 back-to-back calls per graph (serving-like). - Baseline: vLLM's TileLang pre-finalize kernel (vLLM nightly of 2026-10-08), measured in the same session on the same GPU. | T | NS | TileLang cold (µs) | **this PR cold (µs)** | speedup | TileLang warm (µs) | **this PR warm (µs)** | speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 8 | 5.376 | **2.752** | 1.95× | 5.152 | **2.144** | 2.40× | | 2 | 8 | 4.992 | **2.592** | 1.93× | 4.704 | **2.224** | 2.12× | | 4 | 8 | 5.184 | **2.912** | 1.78× | 4.736 | **2.240** | 2.11× | | 8 | 8 | 5.216 | **2.912** | 1.79× | 5.088 | **2.272** | 2.24× | | 16 | 8 | 5.248 | **3.008** | 1.74× | 5.184 | **2.400** | 2.16× | | 24 | 8 | 5.280 | **3.136** | 1.68× | 5.216 | **2.432** | 2.14× | | 32 | 8 | 5.280 | **3.200** | 1.65× | 5.024 | **2.464** | 2.04× | | 1 | 64 | 6.112 | **2.976** | 2.05× | 5.472 | **2.304** | 2.38× | | 2 | 64 | 5.936 | **3.040** | 1.95× | 5.056 | **2.432** | 2.08× | | 4 | 64 | 5.664 | **3.200** | 1.77× | 5.088 | **2.592** | 1.96× | | 8 | 64 | 6.112 | **3.328** | 1.84× | 5.408 | **2.624** | 2.06× | | 16 | 64 | 6.144 | **3.392** | 1.81× | 5.536 | **2.577** | 2.15× | | 24 | 64 | 6.016 | **3.488** | 1.72× | 5.568 | **2.608** | 2.13× | | 32 | 64 | 6.112 | **3.616** | 1.69× | 5.344 | **2.624** | 2.04× | | **geomean** | | 5.604 | **3.099** | **1.81×** | 5.178 | **2.419** | **2.14×** | **Per decode step** (nsys, c=1, 90 calls per step) | per decode step | before | after | change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | mHC pre-finalize | 0.433 ms | 0.239 ms | **−0.195 ms** | | `mhc_fused` (unchanged) | 0.516 ms | 0.515 ms | −0.001 ms | **End to end** (vLLM) - In the baseline arm, `FLASHINFER_SPECIALIZED_KERNEL_DISABLE=1` makes `_supported()` return False, so vLLM keeps its TileLang kernel. | concurrency | mean ITL before → after | mean ITL | ITL p50 | ITL p99 | TTFT p50 | output tok/s | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 4.457 → 4.134 ms | **−7.2%** | −5.4% | −7.0% | −6.7% | **+3.2%** | | 8 (2 pairs pooled) | 5.547 → 5.299 ms | **−4.5%** | −5.4% | −7.1% | +9.0%¹ | −0.4% | | 64 | 15.477 → 15.044 ms | **−2.8%** | −3.8% | +6.1% | −6.2% | **+2.1%** | ¹ Prefill runs identical code in both arms; one of the two allocations was slower at prefill. (A pytest ::selector is not # supported -- the sharding runner cannot consume one.) Must be under # tests/experimental/ and must exist. Delete these comment lines and add yours, e.g. # # tests/experimental/test_my_backend.py # tests/experimental/my_backend/ # # Declaring the whole tree (tests/experimental/) is allowed but means every # experimental PR pays for every other feature's tests, in every matrix cell. ``` ## Reviewer Notes ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added an experimental mHC pre-map operation with fused RMSNorm. +# Experimental mHC pre big-fuse with fused RMSNorm
+
+`flashinfer.mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm` is an **experimental API** with an
+experimental implementation. It is the last step of a manifold-constrained
+hyper-connection (mHC) boundary with `HC = 4` residual streams, in the decode
+regime of models that use mHC. The op consumes the split-K partials of the mHC
+mix projection, so it runs right after the kernel that produces them. It
+returns the mixing coefficients for the next boundary and the RMSNorm'd input
+of the next sublayer:
+
+```
+rms         = rsqrt(sum_s gemm_out_sqrsum[s] / (4 H) + rms_eps)
+mixes       = (sum_s gemm_out_mul[s]) * rms
+pre         = sigmoid(mixes[0:4] * hc_scale[0] + hc_base[0:4]) + hc_pre_eps
+post_mix    = sigmoid(mixes[4:8] * hc_scale[1] + hc_base[4:8]) * hc_post_mult_value
+comb_mix    = sinkhorn_repeat-iteration Sinkhorn of
+              softmax(mixes[8:24].view(4, 4) * hc_scale[2] + hc_base[8:24]) + hc_sinkhorn_eps
+ol          = sum_j pre[j] * residual[:, j]                                   (fp32)
+layer_input = bf16(float(bf16(ol)) * rsqrt(mean(ol^2) + norm_eps) * norm_weight)
+```
+
+It differs from the stable `mhc_pre_big_fuse` in its contract: the output
+RMSNorm (`norm_weight`, `norm_eps`) is fused into `layer_input`, and the split
+count is read from the leading dimension of the partials.
+
+The experimental lifecycle is owned by `@nv-yunzheq` and tracked in issue #TODO.
+
+## Inputs and outputs
+
+| Tensor | dtype | Shape |
+|---|---|---|
+| `gemm_out_mul` | fp32 | `[NS, T, 24]` |
+| `gemm_out_sqrsum` | fp32 | `[NS, T]` |
+| `hc_scale` / `hc_base` | fp32 | `[3]` / `[24]` |
+| `residual` | bf16 | `[T, 4, H]` |
+| `norm_weight` | bf16 | `[H]` |
+| `post_mix` (out) | fp32 | `[T, 4]` |
+| `comb_mix` (out) | fp32 | `[T, 16]` (or a caller-owned `[T, 4, 4]`) |
+| `layer_input` (out) | bf16 | `[T, H]` |
+
+The outputs are allocated when omitted. The model constants have no defaults,
+because they are part of the numerical contract.
+
+## Implementations
+
+- **Cluster kernel** (`csrc/mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_cluster.cu`, SM100 /
+  SM103). It covers `H = 4096`, `1 <= T <= 32` and `NS` in `{8, 64}`. Its
+  compiled-in constants are `rms_eps = norm_eps = 1e-5`,
+  `hc_pre_eps = hc_sinkhorn_eps = 1e-6`, `hc_post_mult_value = 2` and
+  `sinkhorn_repeat = 20`; the support check compares these as fp32. Inputs and
+  outputs must be dense, contiguous and 16-byte aligned.
+  - Each token runs on one thread-block cluster: 4 CTAs, or 2 CTAs when
+    `T > 24`. Each CTA owns 1024 channels.
+  - Two warps per CTA collapse the four bf16 streams. They all-gather the
+    `sum(ol^2)` partials over distributed shared memory (`st.async` +
+    `mbarrier`), then apply the RMSNorm.
+  - Warp 0 of CTA rank 1 computes the softmax and a division-free 20-iteration
+    Sinkhorn. Warp 0 of the post rank writes `post_mix`.
+  - `enable_pdl=True` launches with programmatic dependent launch. The kernel
+    reads no input before `griddepcontrol.wait`.
+- **Composable implementation** (`backend.composable`). An fp32 PyTorch
+  implementation of the contract for any `NS`, `T` and `H`. It serves every
+  call outside the kernel's envelope, so the API always returns a result.
+
+`mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_supported(...)` reports which path a call takes.
+Callers that have their own fast path for the op should keep it whenever this
+returns `False`.
+
+### Numerics
+
+The module is compiled without `-use_fast_math`:
+
+- `expf` is libdevice, and the post sigmoid uses IEEE division.
+- The pre sigmoids and the final Sinkhorn `1/G` use Newton-refined reciprocals.
+- `rsqrt.approx` is applied only to arguments `>= 1e-5`.
+- fp32 add, mul and fma never flush to zero.
+
+The Sinkhorn is kept in diagonal-scaling form `c = r K s / G`:
+
+- Cofactor products replace the per-step divisions.
+- The common denominator is renormalised by an exact power of two.
+- An exact power-of-two rebalance of `r` and `s` after every column half-step
+  keeps both within `(2^-64, 2^50)` for every finite input.
+
+`comb_mix` is therefore finite for all finite logits, including the extreme
+patterns in the tests.
+
+Against the composable implementation, the kernel holds these tolerances:
+
+| Output | atol | rtol / bound |
+|---|---|---|
+| `post_mix` | `2e-6` | rtol `2e-6` |
+| `comb_mix` | `1e-7` | rtol `1e-5` |
+| `layer_input` | — | within `2^-5` relative, and at least 99.5% bit-identical |
+
+## Opt-in, gating and routing
+
+- Calling `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm`, `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_supported`
+  or `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_warmup` is the opt-in. Each warns once with an
+  `ExperimentalWarning`; no environment variable is needed.
+- The op does not take part in any automatic routing: no stable API dispatches
+  to it, and it has no autotuning or trace-apply support.
+  `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS` has no effect on it.
+- `FLASHINFER_SPECIALIZED_KERNEL_DISABLE=1`, read at call time, forces the
+  composable implementation.
+- The kernel is JIT-only. It is not part of the `flashinfer-jit-cache` /
+  `flashinfer-cubin` packages.
+
+## CUDA graphs
+
+The kernel module is never built during CUDA-graph capture. A capturing call
+made before the module is loaded captures the composable implementation.
+
+Call `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_warmup()` before capture to build and load the
+kernel. Pass caller-owned `post_mix`, `comb_mix` and `layer_input` buffers to
+captured calls.
+
+## Limitations
+
+- The kernel targets SM100 / SM103 only. It has been validated on GB300
+  (SM103); SM100 is compiled but not separately validated.
+- The kernel covers `H = 4096` and `HC = 4` only, with the constants listed
+  above. Prefill-sized batches (`T > 32`) and other models' constants run the
+  composable implementation, which is much slower.
+- The kernel supports `NS` in `{8, 64}`.
+
+## Example and tests
+
+```bash
+python examples/experimental/mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm.py --tokens 4 --num-splits 8
+pytest tests/experimental/test_mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm.py
+```
+
+## Graduation
+
+Graduation requires:
+
+- an agreed placement next to the stable `mhc_pre_big_fuse` APIs (a variant
+  flag versus a separate function);
+- runtime constants in place of the compiled-in model constants, or a
+  per-constant-set specialization;
+- validation on SM100;
+- a trace template.

+#
+# The split-K partials of the mHC mix projection (``gemm_out_mul`` [NS, T, 24],
+# ``gemm_out_sqrsum`` [NS, T]) plus the residual streams [T, 4, H] and the next
+# sublayer's RMSNorm weight [H] go in; ``post_mix`` [T, 4], ``comb_mix`` [T, 16]
+# (row-major 4x4) and the RMSNorm'd ``layer_input`` [T, H] (bf16) come out. For
+# H = 4096 on SM100 / SM103 a thread-block-cluster kernel spreads every token
+# over 4 CTAs (2 CTAs for T > 24; decode regime, T <= 32, NS in {8, 64}); every
+# other call runs the composable fp32 torch implementation below, which is the
+# arithmetic contract of the op.
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import struct
+import threading
+from typing import Optional
+
+import torch
+
+from ...jit.core import logger
+from .jit import gen_mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_module
+
+# ``1`` makes every call skip the cluster kernel and run the composable
+# implementation (read at call time, for A/B testing the kernel).
+KILL_SWITCH_ENV = "FLASHINFER_SPECIALIZED_KERNEL_DISABLE"
+
+# What the cluster kernel is compiled for. The model constants are compile-time
+# constants of the kernel and are compared as fp32; calls outside this set run
+# the composable implementation.
+HIDDEN_SIZE = 4096
+HC_MULT = 4
+MIX = HC_MULT * (2 + HC_MULT)
+NUM_SPLITS = frozenset({8, 64})
+MIN_TOKENS = 1
+MAX_TOKENS = 32
+COMPUTE_CAPABILITIES = frozenset({(10, 0), (10, 3)})
+CONSTANTS = {
+    "rms_eps": 1e-5,
+    "hc_pre_eps": 1e-6,
+    "hc_sinkhorn_eps": 1e-6,
+    "hc_post_mult_value": 2.0,
+    "sinkhorn_repeat": 20,
+    "norm_eps": 1e-5,
+}
+
+
+def _fp32(value: float) -> float:
+    return struct.unpack("f", struct.pack("f", float(value)))[0]
+
+
+_CONSTANTS_FP32 = {k: _fp32(v) for k, v in CONSTANTS.items() if k != "sinkhorn_repeat"}
+
+_lock = threading.Lock()
+_state: dict = {"module": None, "module_error": None}
+_device_capability: dict = {}
+# Call counters (kernel calls, composable calls and the reason of every
+# rejected support check), for debugging and tests.
+STATS: dict = {"kernel_calls": 0, "composable_calls": 0, "rejects": {}}
+
+
+def _reject(reason: str) -> bool:
+    rejects = STATS["rejects"]
+    rejects[reason] = rejects.get(reason, 0) + 1
+    return False
+
+
+def _is_capturing() -> bool:
+    try:
+        return bool(torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing())
+    except Exception:
+        return False
+
+
+def _load_module():
+    """Build / load the cluster kernel once (never during CUDA-graph capture)."""
+    if _state["module"] is not None:
+        return _state["module"]
+    if _state["module_error"] is not None:
+        return None
+    with _lock:
+        if _state["module"] is None and _state["module_error"] is None:
+            try:
+                _state["module"] = (
+                    gen_mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_module().build_and_load()
+                )
+            except Exception as exc:  # the composable path keeps the op working
+                message = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
+                _state["module_error"] = message
+                logger.warning(
+                    "mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm: cluster kernel unavailable, "
+                    f"using the composable implementation ({message[:2000]})"
+                )
+    return _state["module"]
+
+
+def _capability_for(device: torch.device, capturing: bool) -> Optional[tuple]:
+    index = device.index if device.index is not None else torch.cuda.current_device()
+    capability = _device_capability.get(index)
+    if capability is None and not capturing:
+        capability = tuple(torch.cuda.get_device_capability(index))
+        _device_capability[index] = capability
+    return capability
+
+
+def _dense(t: Optional[torch.Tensor], shape: tuple, dtype: torch.dtype) -> bool:
+    return (
+        isinstance(t, torch.Tensor)
+        and t.dtype == dtype
+        and tuple(t.shape) == shape
+        and t.is_contiguous()
+    )
+
+
+def supported(
+    gemm_out_mul: torch.Tensor,
+    gemm_out_sqrsum: torch.Tensor,
+    hc_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    hc_base: torch.Tensor,
+    residual: torch.Tensor,
+    norm_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    rms_eps: float,
+    hc_pre_eps: float,
+    hc_sinkhorn_eps: float,
+    hc_post_mult_value: float,
+    sinkhorn_repeat: int,
+    norm_eps: float,
+    post_mix: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    comb_mix: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    layer_input: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,

+    """Return True when :func:`run` launches the cluster kernel for these arguments."""
+    if os.environ.get(KILL_SWITCH_ENV, "") == "1":
+        return _reject("kill_switch")
+    # cheap shape rejects first (callers may probe every call, decode or not)
+    if not isinstance(gemm_out_mul, torch.Tensor) or gemm_out_mul.dim() != 3:

+        return _reject("shape")
+    if ns not in NUM_SPLITS:
+        return _reject("num_splits")
+    if not MIN_TOKENS <= t_tokens <= MAX_TOKENS:
+        return _reject("num_tokens")

+        or _fp32(hc_pre_eps) != _CONSTANTS_FP32["hc_pre_eps"]
+        or _fp32(hc_sinkhorn_eps) != _CONSTANTS_FP32["hc_sinkhorn_eps"]
+        or _fp32(hc_post_mult_value) != _CONSTANTS_FP32["hc_post_mult_value"]
+        or _fp32(norm_eps) != _CONSTANTS_FP32["norm_eps"]
+        or int(sinkhorn_repeat) != CONSTANTS["sinkhorn_repeat"]

+    t_tokens, hc, hidden = residual.shape
+    device = residual.device

+        post_mix = torch.empty((t_tokens, hc), dtype=torch.float32, device=device)

+        comb_mix = torch.empty((t_tokens, hc * hc), dtype=torch.float32, device=device)

+def _kill_switch_unset(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.delenv(KILL_SWITCH, raising=False)

+def _require_sm10x() -> None:
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA required")
+    if get_compute_capability(torch.device("cuda")) not in backend.COMPUTE_CAPABILITIES:
+        pytest.skip(
+            "the mHC pre big-fuse + RMSNorm cluster kernel targets SM100 / SM103"
+        )
+
+
+def _inputs(t: int, ns: int, seed: int = 0, device: str = "cuda"):
+    g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(seed * 7919 + t * 131 + ns)
+    amp = torch.exp(
+        torch.empty(t, 1, 1, device=device).uniform_(-3.9, 0.7, generator=g)
+    )
+    new_r = torch.randn(t, HC, H, device=device, generator=g) * amp
+    residual = new_r.to(torch.bfloat16)
+    fn = torch.randn(MIX, HC * H, device=device, generator=g) * 0.03
+    xs = new_r.reshape(t, HC, ns, H // ns)
+    fs = fn.view(MIX, HC, ns, H // ns)
+    gemm_out_mul = torch.einsum("tjsk,njsk->stn", xs, fs).contiguous()
+    gemm_out_sqrsum = xs.square().sum(dim=(1, 3)).transpose(0, 1).contiguous()
+    hc_scale = torch.tensor([0.09, 0.16, 0.21], device=device)
+    hc_base = torch.randn(MIX, device=device, generator=g)
+    norm_weight = (0.2 + 0.01 * torch.randn(H, device=device, generator=g)).to(
+        torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    return dict(
+        gemm_out_mul=gemm_out_mul,
+        gemm_out_sqrsum=gemm_out_sqrsum,
+        hc_scale=hc_scale,
+        hc_base=hc_base,
+        residual=residual,
+        norm_weight=norm_weight,
+    )
+
+
+def _sinkhorn_fp64(logits: torch.Tensor, eps: float = 1e-6, repeat: int = 20):
+    x = logits.double().reshape(-1, HC, HC)
+    c = torch.softmax(x, dim=-1) + eps
+    c = c / (c.sum(dim=-2, keepdim=True) + eps)
+    for _ in range(repeat - 1):
+        c = c / (c.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + eps)
+        c = c / (c.sum(dim=-2, keepdim=True) + eps)
+    return c.reshape(-1, HC * HC)
+
+
+def _reference_fp64(inp: dict, consts: dict):
+    """float64 evaluation of the op contract (bf16 rounding of ol kept, as in the contract)."""
+    f64 = torch.float64
+    residual = inp["residual"].to(f64)
+    t_tokens = residual.shape[0]
+    sq = inp["gemm_out_sqrsum"].to(f64).sum(dim=0)
+    rms = torch.rsqrt(sq / (HC * H) + consts["rms_eps"])
+    mixes = inp["gemm_out_mul"].to(f64).sum(dim=0) * rms.unsqueeze(-1)
+    scale = inp["hc_scale"].to(f64)
+    base = inp["hc_base"].to(f64)
+    pre = torch.sigmoid(mixes[:, :HC] * scale[0] + base[:HC]) + consts["hc_pre_eps"]
+    post = (
+        torch.sigmoid(mixes[:, HC : 2 * HC] * scale[1] + base[HC : 2 * HC])
+        * consts["hc_post_mult_value"]
+    )
+    comb = _sinkhorn_fp64(
+        mixes[:, 2 * HC :] * scale[2] + base[2 * HC :],
+        consts["hc_sinkhorn_eps"],
+        consts["sinkhorn_repeat"],
+    )
+    ol = (pre.unsqueeze(-1) * residual).sum(dim=1)
+    r = torch.rsqrt(ol.square().mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + consts["norm_eps"])
+    li = ol.to(torch.bfloat16).to(f64) * r * inp["norm_weight"].to(f64)
+    return post, comb.reshape(t_tokens, HC * HC), li
+
+
+def _check(out, ref):
+    post, comb, li = out
+    rpost, rcomb, rli = ref
+    torch.testing.assert_close(post, rpost, atol=2e-6, rtol=2e-6)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(comb, rcomb, atol=1e-7, rtol=1e-5)
+    err = (li.float() - rli.float()).abs()
+    assert bool((err <= 1e-6 + 2.0**-5 * rli.float().abs()).all())
+    exact = (li.view(torch.int16) == rli.view(torch.int16)).float().mean().item()
+    assert exact >= 0.995, exact
+
+
+def _reject_count(reason: str) -> int:
+    return backend.STATS["rejects"].get(reason, 0)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- any host (no GPU needed) ------
+

+def test_api_is_experimental():
+    for fn in (
+        mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm,
+        mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_supported,
+        mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_warmup,
+    ):
+        assert getattr(fn, "is_experimental", False), fn.__name__
+
+
+def test_core_import_does_not_load_the_backend():
+    code = (
+        "import sys, flashinfer, flashinfer.mhc; "
+        "assert 'flashinfer.experimental.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm' not in sys.modules"
+    )
+    subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], check=True)
+
+
+def test_support_envelope_matches_the_kernel_constants():
+    src = (
+        Path(backend.__file__).parent / "csrc" / "mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_cluster.cu"
+    ).read_text()
+
+    def constexpr(name: str) -> float:
+        m = re.search(rf"constexpr (?:int|float) {name} = ([0-9.e+-]+)f?;", src)
+        assert m is not None, name
+        return float(m.group(1))
+
+    assert constexpr("H") == backend.HIDDEN_SIZE == H
+    assert constexpr("HC") == backend.HC_MULT == HC
+    assert constexpr("RMS_EPS") == backend.CONSTANTS["rms_eps"] == CONSTS["rms_eps"]
+    assert constexpr("HC_PRE_EPS") == backend.CONSTANTS["hc_pre_eps"]
+    assert constexpr("SK_EPS") == backend.CONSTANTS["hc_sinkhorn_eps"]
+    assert constexpr("POST_MULT") == backend.CONSTANTS["hc_post_mult_value"]
+    assert constexpr("NORM_EPS") == backend.CONSTANTS["norm_eps"] == CONSTS["norm_eps"]
+    assert backend.CONSTANTS == CONSTS
+    assert sorted(backend.NUM_SPLITS) == [8, 64]
+    assert (backend.MIN_TOKENS, backend.MAX_TOKENS) == (1, 32)
+
+
+def test_support_rejects_before_touching_the_device():
+    # CPU tensors: every semantic / shape / layout check runs before the device check.
+    inp = _inputs(2, 8, device="cpu")
+    cases = [
+        ("num_tokens", dict(inp, **_inputs(33, 8, device="cpu")), CONSTS),
+        ("num_splits", dict(inp, **_inputs(2, 16, device="cpu")), CONSTS),
+        ("constants", inp, dict(CONSTS, hc_post_mult_value=1.0)),
+        ("constants", inp, dict(CONSTS, sinkhorn_repeat=19)),
+        ("no_norm_weight", dict(inp, norm_weight=None), CONSTS),
+        (
+            "input_layout",
+            dict(
+                inp,
+                residual=inp["residual"].transpose(0, 1).contiguous().transpose(0, 1),
+            ),
+            CONSTS,
+        ),  # fmt: skip
+        ("device", inp, CONSTS),
+    ]
+    for reason, args, consts in cases:
+        before = _reject_count(reason)
+        assert not mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_supported(**args, **consts)
+        assert _reject_count(reason) == before + 1, reason
+    misaligned = torch.empty(2 * HC * HC + 1, dtype=torch.float32)[1:].view(2, HC * HC)
+    before = _reject_count("alignment")
+    assert not mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_supported(
+        **inp, **CONSTS, comb_mix=misaligned
+    )
+    assert _reject_count("alignment") == before + 1
+
+
+def test_kill_switch_is_read_at_call_time(monkeypatch):
+    inp = _inputs(1, 8, device="cpu")
+    monkeypatch.setenv(KILL_SWITCH, "1")
+    before = _reject_count("kill_switch")
+    assert not mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_supported(**inp, **CONSTS)
+    assert _reject_count("kill_switch") == before + 1
+    monkeypatch.delenv(KILL_SWITCH)
+    mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_supported(**inp, **CONSTS)
+    assert _reject_count("kill_switch") == before + 1
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("t,ns", [(1, 8), (3, 8), (5, 64), (40, 4)])
+def test_composable_path_matches_fp64_reference(t, ns):
+    inp = _inputs(t, ns, seed=t, device="cpu")
+    before = backend.STATS["composable_calls"]
+    out = mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm(**inp, **CONSTS)
+    assert backend.STATS["composable_calls"] == before + 1
+    post, comb, li = out
+    assert post.shape == (t, HC) and post.dtype == torch.float32
+    assert comb.shape == (t, HC * HC) and comb.dtype == torch.float32
+    assert li.shape == (t, H) and li.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    rpost, rcomb, rli = _reference_fp64(inp, CONSTS)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(post.double(), rpost, atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(comb.double(), rcomb, atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-5)
+    # layer_input: bf16(ol) may round one ulp apart, plus the final bf16 rounding
+    err = (li.double() - rli).abs()
+    assert bool((err <= 1e-6 + 2.0**-6 * rli.abs()).all())
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- SM100 / SM103 GPUs ------------
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("t", [1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 13, 16, 24, 25, 31, 32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("ns", [8, 64])
+def test_kernel_matches_composable(t, ns, monkeypatch):
+    _require_sm10x()
+    inp = _inputs(t, ns)
+    assert mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_supported(**inp, **CONSTS)
+    before = backend.STATS["kernel_calls"]
+    out = mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm(**inp, **CONSTS)
+    assert backend.STATS["kernel_calls"] == before + 1
+    monkeypatch.setenv(KILL_SWITCH, "1")
+    assert not mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_supported(**inp, **CONSTS)
+    ref = mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm(**inp, **CONSTS)
+    _check(out, ref)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enable_pdl", [False, True])
+def test_sinkhorn_extreme_comb_logits(enable_pdl):
+    # The comb logits are injected through hc_base with hc_scale[2] = 0, so they are exactly
+    # the rows above; comb_mix must be finite and match a float64 Sinkhorn.
+    _require_sm10x()
+    for ns in (8, 64):
+        for name, row in EXTREME_COMB_LOGITS.items():
+            logits = torch.tensor(row, dtype=torch.float32)
+            inp = _inputs(2, ns)
+            inp["hc_scale"][2] = 0.0
+            inp["hc_base"][2 * HC :] = logits.cuda()
+            assert mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_supported(**inp, **CONSTS)
+            _, comb, _ = mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm(
+                **inp, **CONSTS, enable_pdl=enable_pdl
+            )
+            ref = _sinkhorn_fp64(logits)
+            got = comb.double().cpu()
+            assert torch.isfinite(got).all(), name
+            bound = 1e-7 + 1e-5 * ref.abs()
+            assert bool(((got - ref).abs() <= bound).all()), name
+
+
+def test_unsupported_calls_take_composable_path():
+    _require_sm10x()
+    inp = _inputs(33, 8)
+    assert not mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_supported(**inp, **CONSTS)
+    before = backend.STATS["composable_calls"]
+    mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm(**inp, **CONSTS)
+    assert backend.STATS["composable_calls"] == before + 1
+    consts = dict(CONSTS, hc_post_mult_value=1.0)
+    assert not mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_supported(**_inputs(2, 8), **consts)
+
+
+def _graph_outputs(t):
+    return tuple(
+        torch.empty(s, dtype=d, device="cuda")
+        for s, d in (
+            ((t, HC), torch.float32),
+            ((t, HC * HC), torch.float32),
+            ((t, H), torch.bfloat16),
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def test_cuda_graph_capture_after_warmup(monkeypatch):
+    _require_sm10x()
+    assert mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_warmup(torch.device("cuda"))
+    inp = _inputs(2, 8)
+    outs = _graph_outputs(2)
+    before = backend.STATS["kernel_calls"]
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm(
+            **inp, **CONSTS, post_mix=outs[0], comb_mix=outs[1], layer_input=outs[2]
+        )
+    assert backend.STATS["kernel_calls"] == before + 1
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    monkeypatch.setenv(KILL_SWITCH, "1")
+    ref = mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm(**inp, **CONSTS)
+    _check(outs, ref)
+
+
+def test_cuda_graph_capture_without_loaded_module_falls_back(monkeypatch):
+    # A capturing call never builds or loads the module: it captures the composable path.
+    _require_sm10x()
+    assert mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_warmup(torch.device("cuda"))
+    monkeypatch.setitem(backend._state, "module", None)
+    inp = _inputs(2, 8)
+    outs = _graph_outputs(2)
+    unready = _reject_count("capture_unready")
+    kernel_calls = backend.STATS["kernel_calls"]
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm(
+            **inp, **CONSTS, post_mix=outs[0], comb_mix=outs[1], layer_input=outs[2]
+        )
+    assert _reject_count("capture_unready") == unready + 1
+    assert backend.STATS["kernel_calls"] == kernel_calls
+    assert backend._state["module"] is None
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    monkeypatch.setenv(KILL_SWITCH, "1")
+    _check(outs, mhc.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm(**inp, **CONSTS))
